title_en: Notice of the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security on Effectively Solving the Problems of Early Departure from Posts and Resignation of Judges and Prosecutors
full_text_en:
Organization Department of the Communist Party of China Central Committee  Supreme People's Court

Supreme People's Procuratorate  Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security

Notice on Effectively Resolving the Issues of Judges and Prosecutors Leaving Posts Early or Resigning

Fa Fa [2010] No. 14

The Organization Departments of the Party Committees of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, the High People's Courts, the People's Procuratorates, the Departments (Bureaus) of Human Resources and Social Security; the Organization Department of the Party Committee of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, the Personnel Bureau; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, the People's Procuratorate of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

In recent years, there has been a widespread phenomenon of judges and prosecutors in local people's courts and people's procuratorates at all levels leaving their posts early or resigning. To a certain extent, this has exacerbated the contradiction of having more cases than personnel in the people's courts and people's procuratorates, and has also increased the difficulty of team management. In order to implement the requirement of the Fourth Plenary Session of the Seventeenth Central Committee of the Communist Party of China regarding "making reasonable use of cadres of all ages and effectively solving the problem of the progressive reduction of the age limit for leading cadres to assume office", and to further strengthen the team building of the people's courts and people's procuratorates, based on the professional characteristics of judges and prosecutors, the following notice is hereby given on effectively resolving the issues of judges and prosecutors leaving posts early or resigning:

1. Strictly implement the state's provisions on the retirement age for civil servants. From now on, judges and prosecutors who have not reached the retirement age shall not be forced to leave their posts early for recuperation, nor shall they simply be divided by age limits to cause judges and prosecutors holding leadership positions in the court or in internal organs to change to non-leadership positions. Judges and prosecutors who have not reached retirement age and no longer hold leadership positions may be changed to adjudicators or procurators at the same level of post, and continue to engage in case handling work.

2. For personnel who meet the conditions for early retirement and voluntarily retire early, approval shall be strictly granted in accordance with the authority for cadre management.

3. People's courts and people's procuratorates at all levels shall fully utilize the advantages of the experienced and professionally skilled judges and prosecutors who have already left their posts early or resigned. Based on the management characteristics after early departure or resignation, they shall scientifically and reasonably arrange their work content.

4. People's courts and people's procuratorates at all levels shall, strictly in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Servant Law, the Judges Law, and the Procurators Law, manage and assess judges and prosecutors who have already left their posts early or resigned, clarify attendance discipline, and require them to perform their work duties normally.

5. Judges and prosecutors who have already left their posts early or resigned shall strictly comply with relevant regulations and shall not engage in legal services such as acting as litigation representatives or defense counsel. People's courts and people's procuratorates at all levels shall adopt strict supervision and implementation measures.

6. To alleviate the prominent contradiction of having more cases than personnel in the people's courts and people's procuratorates in the eastern region and the shortage of judges and prosecutors in the central and western regions, local people's courts and people's procuratorates at all levels may, based on local actual conditions, organize retired judges and prosecutors in good health from their own institutions to assist with work.

7. Local organization and personnel departments at all levels, as well as people's courts and people's procuratorates, shall strictly implement the provisions of this notice, and relevant higher-level departments shall strengthen supervision and inspection. Any violation of the provisions of this notice shall be immediately and resolutely corrected. If corrections are not made in a timely manner, the responsible persons shall be held accountable.

8. This notice shall come into effect as of the date of issuance.

May 12, 2010
